title: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 formally deprecated and must not be negotiated
summary: Normative TLS baseline for lower-layer configuration checks. Any source that still permits TLS 1.0 or 1.1 creates drift from the standard.

title: Bearer tokens without sender constraint are replayable by design
summary: Bearer tokens grant access to whoever holds them. DPoP or mTLS binding is needed to prevent token replay after exfiltration.

title: Wildcard origin with credentials is rejected by browsers
summary: Authenticated browser APIs need explicit origin allowlists. Wildcard CORS is only valid for public resources without credentials.

title: JWT 'none' algorithm must be rejected by all validators
summary: The 'none' algorithm bypass is a known attack vector. Libraries must enforce algorithm allowlists and reject unsigned tokens.

title: PSTN out-of-band auth is restricted at AAL2 and cannot satisfy AAL3
summary: SMS OTP can be acceptable only inside a documented assurance boundary. Stronger auth is needed for AAL3 targets.

title: TLS server certificates must use RSA 2048+ or ECDSA P-256+
summary: Certificate key sizes below the threshold are non-compliant. Automated certificate management should enforce minimum key parameters.

title: Secrets must not be stored in source control
summary: Prefer workload identity and temporary credentials. Static secrets need controlled storage, rotation, audit, and revocation.

title: Session tokens must be invalidated on logout and password change
summary: Server-side session invalidation prevents token reuse. JWTs require explicit revocation lists or short expiry with rotation.

title: DELETE and PUT are not safe methods and must not be cached
summary: HTTP method semantics define caching and safety properties. Middleware must respect method classification for security decisions.

title: SHA-1 is disallowed for digital signatures
summary: SHA-1 collision attacks are practical. All signing operations must use SHA-256 or stronger. Legacy systems need migration plans.

title: TLS 1.3 removes static RSA key exchange and compression
summary: Forward secrecy is mandatory in TLS 1.3. Systems negotiating TLS 1.2 should prefer ECDHE cipher suites.

title: Broken access control is the #1 web application risk
summary: Access control failures outnumber injection in current data. Server-side enforcement and deny-by-default are baseline requirements.

title: JWK key sets must validate key use and algorithm constraints
summary: Accepting any key from a JWKS endpoint without checking 'use' and 'alg' fields enables key confusion attacks.

title: Least privilege must be enforced for all system accounts
summary: Administrative access must be scoped and time-limited. Standing privileges create persistent attack surface.

title: Authorization code interception requires PKCE mitigation
summary: Public clients cannot protect client secrets. PKCE binds the authorization code to the requesting client.

title: Object-level authorization must be checked on every request
summary: BOLA is the most common API vulnerability. Resource identifiers must be validated against the authenticated caller's permissions.

title: Error responses should not leak internal implementation details
summary: Structured error responses help clients. Stack traces, SQL errors, and internal paths must be filtered from production responses.

title: Container images must be scanned and signed before deployment
summary: Unsigned or unscanned images bypass supply chain controls. Admission policies should enforce image provenance.

title: CloudTrail console and IaC paths create different trail scope
summary: Console-created trails can differ from CLI, API, CloudFormation, or CDK trails unless multi-region scope is explicit.

title: IAM Identity Center is the centralized workforce access pattern
summary: Architecture guidance aligns with federation and temporary credentials. Drift remains where legacy user-key tutorials stay visible.

title: VPC flow logs should be enabled for all production VPCs
summary: Flow logs provide network-level visibility. Without them, lateral movement and data exfiltration lack detection signals.

title: IMDSv2 should be required on EC2 instances
summary: IMDSv1 allows SSRF-to-metadata credential theft. Launch paths should explicitly require session-oriented metadata access.

title: Pod security standards should replace PodSecurityPolicy
summary: PSP is removed in K8s 1.25. Migration to Pod Security Admission or policy engines is required for enforcement.

title: S3 Block Public Access should be enabled at account level
summary: Account-level BPA prevents accidental public bucket creation. Bucket-level overrides should require explicit exception process.

title: Security Hub standards should be enabled in all regions
summary: Security Hub is regional. Findings from unused regions can be missed without multi-region enablement.

title: KMS key deletion permissions should be restricted to specific roles
summary: Accidental key deletion causes irreversible data loss. Restrict ScheduleKeyDeletion to specific roles and use the mandatory 7-30 day waiting period.

title: Lambda in VPC requires NAT gateway for internet access
summary: VPC Lambda functions lose internet access without NAT. Console does not warn about this dependency during configuration.

title: WAF rules should be attached to all public-facing distributions
summary: CloudFront distributions without WAF expose origin servers to unfiltered traffic. Default creation flow does not require WAF.

title: Service control policies should deny root user access in member accounts
summary: SCPs provide guardrails across the organization. Root user actions in member accounts bypass IAM policies but respect SCPs.

title: GuardDuty should be enabled in all accounts and regions
summary: GuardDuty threat detection requires explicit enablement per account and region. Gaps create blind spots for compromise detection.

title: Step Functions execution roles should be scoped to specific state machines
summary: Shared execution roles across state machines violate least privilege. Each workflow should have a dedicated role.

title: DynamoDB encryption at rest uses AWS-owned keys by default
summary: AWS-owned keys prevent customer audit of key usage. CMK encryption provides audit trail and rotation control.

title: Cognito user pool should enable threat protection
summary: Threat protection (formerly advanced security features) including adaptive authentication and compromised credential detection is opt-in. Default pools lack brute-force and credential-stuffing protection.

title: SNS topics should enforce encryption and access policies
summary: SNS topics created without resource policies can allow cross-account publish. Server-side encryption should be enabled for sensitive messages.

title: ECR image scanning should be enabled on push for all repositories
summary: Scan-on-push catches known CVEs before deployment. Enhanced scanning with Inspector provides continuous monitoring.

title: SQS default SSE-SQS encryption lacks customer key audit and rotation control
summary: SQS queues use SSE-SQS encryption by default since October 2022. For sensitive data requiring audit trail and key rotation control, SSE-KMS with customer-managed keys should be used.

title: CORS wildcard examples omit credentialed-endpoint restrictions
summary: Docs show wildcard CORS as the default example. Browsers reject wildcard origin with credentials, but the doc does not warn on the same page.

title: Refresh tokens can be configured for long lifetimes
summary: Long token windows are supported configuration, not a recommendation. Threat model and rotation rules need to be explicit.

title: Managed security headers policy is opt-in and omits CSP
summary: Managed policies provide a baseline but must be attached to cache behavior and augmented for CSP and permissions policy.

title: Legacy TLS policies remain selectable as compatibility options
summary: The docs are accurate, but selectable legacy policies can drift from current TLS baselines if copied into new systems.

title: Default Lambda timeout of 3 seconds may cause silent failures
summary: Short default timeout is not a security issue, but silent failure can mask security-relevant processing like token validation.

title: S3 ACLs are disabled by default but still documented as a configurable option
summary: ACLs are off by default (Object Ownership: bucket-owner-enforced). Re-enabling ACLs is still documented and possible, creating drift when older patterns are copied.

title: RDS master password can be stored in Secrets Manager optionally
summary: Console allows plaintext password entry without Secrets Manager integration. Production databases should use managed rotation.

title: Long-lived access keys remain a documented option despite temporary credentials being preferred
summary: Access key docs include rotation guidance but access keys remain a first-class option. Temporary credentials via IAM roles are the recommended pattern.

title: DynamoDB Streams inherit table encryption but key changes require re-creation
summary: Streams inherit the table's encryption key (including CMK). Changing the encryption key on a table does not retroactively re-encrypt existing stream records.

title: EKS cluster endpoint can be public by default
summary: Public API endpoints expose the control plane to the internet. Private endpoint access should be the production default.

title: Log group retention defaults to never expire
summary: Unlimited retention increases storage costs and may violate data retention policies. Explicit retention periods should be set.

title: SNS HTTPS subscriptions require CA-signed certificates but confirmation flow can be spoofed
summary: SNS validates CA-signed certificates by default. However, the subscription confirmation token can be intercepted if the HTTPS endpoint is compromised, granting persistent message delivery.

title: SES sending authorization requires explicit identity policies
summary: Cross-account SES sending requires identity-based and resource-based policy alignment. Missing policies cause silent failures.

title: WAF rate-based rules had a minimum threshold of 100 requests per 5-minute window
summary: The minimum rate limit of 100 requests (lowered to 10 in August 2024) may be too coarse for targeted endpoints. Additional mitigation layers may be needed.

title: DNSSEC signing is opt-in per hosted zone
summary: DNS responses are unsigned by default. DNSSEC prevents cache poisoning but requires careful key rotation management.

title: Config rules evaluate but do not auto-remediate by default
summary: Evaluation without remediation creates alert fatigue. Auto-remediation requires explicit SSM Automation document configuration.

title: Lambda authorizer caching can serve stale auth decisions
summary: Cached authorizer responses persist for the TTL period. Token revocation during cache window is not reflected.

title: Secrets Manager rotation for non-managed secrets requires Lambda function configuration
summary: RDS-managed passwords rotate automatically, but custom secrets require explicit Lambda rotation function configuration or they remain static indefinitely.

title: Sample Lambda roles often exceed least-privilege scope
summary: Convenience permissions in sample code can propagate into production templates when copied without review.

title: Docker examples frequently omit non-root runtime user
summary: A Dockerfile without a USER instruction runs as root by default. Task definitions should also lock down writable filesystems.

title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML examples need sanitizer boundaries
summary: Framework escape hatches bypass default XSS protection. Rich HTML from users needs strict sanitizer allowlists.

title: CDK examples use wildcard resource ARNs in IAM policies
summary: Resource: '*' in sample IAM policies grants access to all resources. Production policies must scope to specific ARNs.

title: Workshop RBAC examples bind cluster-admin to default service account
summary: cluster-admin ClusterRoleBinding in samples creates privilege escalation paths. Workshop cleanup steps often miss RBAC rollback.

title: Terraform S3 backend examples omit state locking configuration
summary: Without DynamoDB state locking, concurrent applies can corrupt state. Sample backends should include lock table configuration.

title: SDK examples catch broad exceptions, risking sensitive data in error output
summary: Broad except-all handlers in sample code can expose request metadata containing sensitive data when exceptions are logged.

title: CFN templates use hardcoded CIDR blocks for security groups
summary: Hardcoded 0.0.0.0/0 ingress rules in sample templates create open security groups when deployed without modification.

title: Sample API endpoints lack request validation
summary: Sample APIs accept any request body without schema validation. API Gateway request validators should be configured.

title: Cognito sample apps store tokens in localStorage
summary: localStorage is accessible to XSS. Tokens should use httpOnly cookies or in-memory storage with refresh token rotation.

title: Step Functions sample workflows pass full event payload between states
summary: Passing entire payloads increases state size and may expose sensitive data in execution history. Use InputPath/ResultPath filtering.

title: DynamoDB samples use Scan instead of Query for filtered reads
summary: Full table scans are expensive and can expose data across partition boundaries. Samples should demonstrate Query with key conditions.

title: VPC sample templates rely on default allow-all network ACLs
summary: Subnets always have a NACL, but samples use the default which allows all traffic. Production templates should define explicit NACL rules.

title: CodePipeline examples use plaintext environment variables for secrets
summary: CodeBuild PLAINTEXT env var type exposes values in build logs. Use PARAMETER_STORE or SECRETS_MANAGER types instead.

title: SQS consumer samples lack dead-letter queue configuration
summary: Without DLQ, failed messages are retried indefinitely or silently dropped. Samples should include redrive policy configuration.

title: KMS sample code uses default key policy allowing root account full access
summary: Default key policy grants root account unrestricted access. Production keys should specify explicit key administrators and users.

title: CloudFront sample origins use S3 website endpoint without OAC
summary: S3 website endpoints cannot use OAC. Samples should use S3 REST endpoints with OAC to prevent direct bucket access.

title: EventBridge samples use overly broad event patterns
summary: Broad event patterns trigger on unintended events. Production rules should match on specific source, detail-type, and detail fields.

title: Community trackers catch permission changes before docs settle
summary: Trackers are not authority, but they surface changes that need confirmation against official service behavior.

title: Observed TLS defaults differ by provisioning path
summary: Console defaults can be stronger than CLI or IaC defaults. Production templates should set policy values explicitly.

title: Community reports surface zero-day patterns before vendor patches
summary: Advisory databases aggregate community vulnerability reports. Dependency scanning should monitor multiple advisory sources.

title: S3 bucket enumeration tools document public bucket discovery techniques
summary: Bucket naming patterns are predictable. Account-level BPA and bucket policies are more reliable than obscurity.

title: RBAC misconfigurations are the most reported K8s security issue
summary: Community reports consistently highlight overprivileged service accounts and missing network policies.

title: Cross-account role assumption chains create transitive trust
summary: Role chaining across accounts can create unintended access paths. Trust policies should use explicit condition keys.

title: Provider updates change default security configurations
summary: Major provider version bumps can change default values for encryption, public access, and logging. Pin versions and review changelogs.

title: Base image vulnerability counts vary significantly between scanners
summary: Scanner databases and detection methods differ. Cross-referencing multiple scanners provides more complete coverage.

title: SSRF to cloud metadata is a recurring attack pattern
summary: SSRF attacks targeting metadata services continue despite IMDSv2. Application-level SSRF prevention is still necessary.

title: API rate limiting bypasses via header manipulation documented
summary: X-Forwarded-For and similar headers can bypass IP-based rate limiting. Rate limits should use authenticated identity where possible.

title: Community SAST rules detect patterns missed by commercial tools
summary: Semgrep and similar tools have community-contributed rules for framework-specific vulnerabilities.

title: Subdomain takeover monitoring reveals dangling DNS records
summary: Dangling CNAME records for decommissioned services can be claimed by attackers. DNS hygiene requires lifecycle management.

title: Prowler findings reveal gaps between documented and actual security posture
summary: Open-source audit tools often check controls not covered by AWS-managed config rules. Multiple audit sources improve coverage.

title: OIDC token validation libraries have inconsistent claim verification
summary: Libraries differ on which claims are validated by default. Audience, issuer, and expiry should be explicitly checked.

title: Push notification fatigue attacks bypass MFA approval
summary: Repeated push notifications can trick users into approving malicious requests. Number matching and rate limiting reduce risk.

title: Versioned S3 objects remain accessible after deletion to any principal with read permissions
summary: Delete operations on versioned buckets insert delete markers but preserve previous versions. Anyone with s3:GetObjectVersion can read 'deleted' data.

title: JWT tutorials use weak shared secrets or hardcoded signing keys
summary: Copied auth snippets often skip key management and rotation. Review generated or tutorial code against current auth guidance.

title: Local Terraform state exposes secrets when committed
summary: Default local state is plaintext JSON. Use remote state with access controls and keep state files out of source control.

title: Quickstarts omit throttling and usage plans
summary: Unauthenticated or authenticated callers can consume backend resources unless stage throttles, usage plans, and rate rules are configured.

title: Public database examples reduce defense-in-depth
summary: Publicly reachable databases still need auth and network rules, but private subnet placement is the safer production baseline.

title: AI code assistants generate security groups with 0.0.0.0/0 ingress
summary: LLM-generated infrastructure code often uses permissive defaults. Security review must cover AI-generated configurations.

title: Tutorials store AWS credentials as GitHub Actions secrets without OIDC
summary: Static credentials in CI/CD are unnecessary with OIDC federation. GitHub Actions can assume roles without long-lived keys.

title: Top-voted answers recommend disabling SSL verification for development
summary: VERIFY_NONE and --insecure flags in accepted answers get copied to production. Development convenience should not compromise production security.

title: CORS tutorials recommend Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * as first solution
summary: Wildcard origin is the most commonly recommended CORS fix. Tutorials rarely distinguish between public and credentialed endpoints.

title: Popular Docker images run as root and include unnecessary packages
summary: Base images with unnecessary packages increase attack surface. Distroless or minimal images with non-root users are preferred.

title: AI-generated code omits input validation and parameterized queries
summary: Generated database queries often use string concatenation. AI output needs security review for injection vulnerabilities.

title: Express.js tutorials omit helmet, rate limiting, and CSRF protection
summary: Minimal Express setups in tutorials lack security middleware. Production apps need explicit security header and rate limit configuration.

title: K8s tutorials use kubectl apply with cluster-admin context
summary: Tutorial kubectl commands assume cluster-admin. Production access should use scoped RBAC and namespace-limited contexts.

title: OAuth tutorials skip state parameter and PKCE implementation
summary: Missing state parameter enables CSRF on OAuth flows. PKCE is required for public clients and recommended for all.

title: Forked workshop repos contain outdated IAM policies with known issues
summary: Workshop forks diverge from maintained originals. Outdated policies in forks propagate known security issues.

title: Blog posts implement custom encryption instead of using AWS KMS
summary: Custom cryptography in application code is error-prone. Managed key services provide audited, standards-compliant encryption.

title: Serverless tutorials use broad IAM permissions with iamRoleStatements
summary: Framework tutorials often grant lambda:* or s3:* permissions for simplicity. Production functions need scoped resource policies.
